headline: KetchUp is an open-source SketchUp alternative built with Rust and WebGPU
summary: KetchUp offers a modern, browser-based 3D modeling experience, leveraging Rust for performance and WebGPU for advanced graphics rendering.
details: KetchUp emerges as a new open-source 3D modeling alternative to SketchUp, built with modern web technologies. It leverages Rust for its robust backend and WebGPU for high-performance graphics rendering directly in the browser.

This combination aims to provide a fast, safe, and efficient modeling environment. Rust's memory safety and performance benefits contribute to a stable application, while WebGPU enables advanced visual effects and real-time rendering capabilities.

SketchUp is renowned for its intuitive interface and accessibility in 3D design, particularly for architectural and interior design. KetchUp seeks to offer a similar user-friendly experience, but with the advantages of an open-source, community-driven development model.

Being browser-based, KetchUp eliminates the need for complex installations, making it accessible across various operating systems and devices. Users can start designing quickly without significant setup overhead.

The open-source nature invites developers and designers to contribute to its growth and feature set. This collaborative approach fosters innovation and ensures the tool evolves based on user needs and community input.

KetchUp is positioned for a wide range of users, from hobbyists and students to professional architects and product designers. Its development is ongoing, with a focus on expanding features and enhancing usability to compete effectively in the 3D modeling space.

headline: Open Transit Software launches free, open-source vehicle tracking after UCSD deployment
summary: The new Vehicle Positions software replaces expensive proprietary systems with free, open-source alternatives running on smartphones. This follows the successful deployment of their Wayfinder and Waystation web apps at UC San Diego for over 35,000 students.
details: The Open Transit Software Foundation has successfully deployed its Wayfinder and Waystation web applications, serving over 35,000 students at the University of California San Diego. These tools aim to improve navigation and access to transit information for a large university population.

The foundation is now preparing to launch its Vehicle Positions software, designed to replace expensive, proprietary vehicle location systems. This new solution offers a free, open-source alternative that operates using commodity smartphones.

In parallel, their next-generation server software, Maglev, is being enhanced to support advanced transit data formats like GTFS-Flex. This upgrade will enable the mapping and display of demand-responsive transit systems, offering greater flexibility.

The Open Transit Software Foundation is actively seeking volunteers across various roles, including developers, business development, UX designers, and product managers. These positions are crucial for continuing the development and expansion of their open-source projects.
